metadata.title: Kling 3 Motion Control AI Video Generator | Reference Motion Transfer
metadata.description: Use Kling 3 Motion Control when exact pose, gesture, and body timing should come from a driving video. Upload one character image, one MP4 or QuickTime motion reference, then generate 720p or 1080p output.

modelIntro.title: What Is Kling 3 Motion Control?
description: Kling 3 Motion Control is the Toolaze Kling 3 flow for motion-reference transfer. The uploaded image defines the character or subject to preserve, while the uploaded video defines the action path, body timing, pose sequence, and camera rhythm.

Choose it when matching a specific movement matters more than writing a broad text-to-video prompt. Use it for clean driving footage, higher-control identity preservation, orientation-aware character movement, and 720p or 1080p output where credits scale with the reference-video length.

metrics.label: Primary job
metrics.value: Transfer motion from a driving video to one uploaded character image.

metrics.label: Required inputs
metrics.value: 1 character image plus 1 motion reference video.

metrics.label: Character image
metrics.value: 1 JPEG, PNG, or JPG image, max 10MB; image size must be greater than 300px with aspect ratio from 2:5 to 5:2.

metrics.label: Motion reference video
metrics.value: 1 MP4 or QuickTime motion reference video, max 100MB. Image orientation supports 3-10 second references; Video orientation supports 3-30 seconds.

metrics.label: Prompt
metrics.value: Optional. Use it to preserve identity, outfit, body proportions, lighting, camera framing, and style. Keep it under 2500 characters.

metrics.label: Character orientation
metrics.value: Choose Image when the uploaded image should define character direction, or Video when the motion reference should define character direction.

metrics.label: Duration
metrics.value: Output duration follows the uploaded motion reference video duration instead of a fixed manual duration.

metrics.label: Credit guidance
metrics.value: Credits scale with the uploaded motion reference video duration; current Toolaze rate is 40 credits per output second at 720p or 54 credits per output second at 1080p.

metrics.label: Not a fit for
metrics.value: Prompt-only video ideas, broad scene generation, 4K output, or clips without a usable motion reference video.

howToUse.title: How To Prepare Kling 3 Motion Control Inputs

steps.title: Pick the character source
steps.desc: Upload one clear JPEG, PNG, or JPG image where the face, body, outfit, or product shape is easy to read.

steps.title: Match the driving motion
steps.desc: Use an MP4 or QuickTime reference video with visible body motion, limited occlusion, and framing close to the character image.

steps.title: Choose character orientation
steps.desc: Use Image orientation when the still image should control direction. Use Video orientation when the reference clip should control direction and can run up to 30 seconds.

steps.title: Keep the prompt protective
steps.desc: Describe what must stay stable: identity, outfit, body proportions, lighting, framing, and style. Avoid asking for scene changes that conflict with the driving video.

scenesTitle: Reference Inputs That Work Best With Kling 3 Motion Control

scenes.title: Full-body motion reference
scenes.desc: Use a driving clip where the whole body stays visible, the pose sequence is easy to follow, and the camera does not cut away mid-action.

scenes.title: Presenter or avatar gesture
scenes.desc: Match portrait crop, body angle, hand visibility, and character orientation when a still presenter or avatar image should follow supplied gestures.

scenes.title: Product-in-hand action
scenes.desc: Use a close, stable hand-motion video for lifting, rotating, tapping, or presenting a product. Avoid blocked limbs, hard cuts, and mismatched camera angles.

faq.q: Who should use Kling 3 Motion Control?
faq.a: Use it when you already have a character image and a driving video, and the output needs to follow that video's pose, gesture, body timing, or camera rhythm.

faq.q: How is Kling 3 Motion Control different from Kling 2.6 Motion Control?
faq.a: Both use one character image and one motion reference video. Kling 3 Motion Control is the newer Toolaze motion-control option with stricter image guidance and higher per-second credits, while Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control remains the lower-cost nearby flow.

faq.q: When should I choose Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control instead?
faq.a: Choose Kling 2.6 when cost is the main constraint, when the 2.6 motion-control flow is already sufficient, or when your source video is Matroska and you do not want to convert it first.

faq.q: Can I create from a prompt only?
faq.a: No. Kling 3 Motion Control requires both a character image and a motion reference video. Use standard Kling 3.0 or another video model for prompt-only generation.

faq.q: What image formats can I upload?
faq.a: Use one JPEG, PNG, or JPG image up to 10MB. The image should be larger than 300px and stay within the 2:5 to 5:2 aspect-ratio range.

faq.q: What video formats can I upload?
faq.a: Use one MP4 or QuickTime motion reference video up to 100MB. Image orientation supports 3-10 second references, while Video orientation supports 3-30 second references.
Image orientation follows the character direction in the uploaded still image. Video orientation follows the character direction in the uploaded motion reference video.
Credits follow the output duration, which comes from the uploaded reference video. The current Toolaze rate is 40 credits per second at 720p or 54 credits per second at 1080p.

faq.q: What makes a good motion reference video?
faq.a: Use clear footage with visible limbs or hands, stable framing, limited occlusion, and motion that matches the character image's angle and crop.

faq.q: What should the optional prompt say?
faq.a: Keep it short and protective: preserve identity, outfit, body proportions, lighting, camera framing, and style while following the uploaded motion reference.
